headline: 'Mind of its own': Raducanu advances despite wayward serve
summary: A rusty Emma Raducanu said her serve felt like it had a mind of its own at times on Tuesday as she racked up 15 double faults in a 7-6(4) 7-6(2) first-round victory over Russian Ekaterina Alexandrova at the Australian Open.

headline: Cummins to lead Australia's big guns at Champions Trophy
summary: Pat Cummins will captain Australia at the Champions Trophy after being named in a preliminary 15-man squad also featuring fellow quick Josh Hazlewood on Tuesday.

headline: Tens of thousands protest in Belgrade
summary: Tens of thousands of anti-government protesters in Belgrade on Sunday switched on the lights on their mobile phones and stood in silence for 15 minutes to commemorate victims of a railway station roof collapse for which they blame authorities.

headline: Tougher U.S. sanctions to curb Russian oil supply to China and India
summary: Chinese and Indian refiners will source more oil from the Middle East, Africa and the Americas, boosting prices and freight costs, as new U.S. sanctions on Russian producers and ships curb supplies to Moscow's top customers, traders and analysts said.

headline: Zelenskiy calls on allies to honour promises on arms supplies to Ukraine
summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiy called on allies on Sunday to honour all promises to supply Ukraine with weapons, including those to counter Russian air attacks.

headline: Indonesia coach Kluivert eyes World Cup qualification
summary: New Indonesia coach Patrick Kluivert wants to lead his team to the 2026 World Cup finals and is looking for a fast start in his first match in charge against Australia.

headline: No. 19 Memphis survives scare to get past East Carolina
summary: PJ Haggerty scored 25 points and No. 19 Memphis offered a definition of an ugly win in defeating visiting East Carolina 74-70 in an American Athletic Conference matchup on Saturday afternoon.

headline: Jeju Air black box data missing from crucial minutes before crash
summary: The discovery of the missing data suggests all power may have been cut, which is rare, a former government accident investigator said.

headline: Collins glad to be back at Australian Open after personal setbacks
summary: Danielle Collins had no intention of being at this year's Australian Open but the former finalist is glad to be back at Melbourne Park and taking comfort in the routines of tennis after personal setbacks.

headline: American Kessler beats Mertens to win Hobart International
summary: McCartney Kessler will head into the Australian Open with a second WTA title under her belt after scoring a 6-4 3-6 6-0 victory over Elise Mertens in the Hobart International final on Saturday.

headline: Packers QB Jordan Love (elbow) set to play vs. Eagles
summary: Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love's right elbow is improving and he didn't receive an injury status for Sunday's NFC wild-card game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

headline: Sydney synagogue sprayed with antisemitic graffiti in latest attack on Australian Jews
summary: A synagogue in Sydney was daubed in antisemitic graffiti, police said on Saturday, a day after the antisemitic vandalism of a separate synagogue in the New South Wales state capital.

headline: Manhattan's top federal prosecutor Williams joins law firm Paul Weiss
summary: Damian Williams, the former top federal prosecutor in Manhattan, will return to law firm Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison as a partner in New York, the firm said on Friday.

headline: AkzoNobel to lay off up to 16% of workforce in France
summary: Dutch paint and coatings maker AkzoNobel plans to lay off of up to 211 staff in France, about 16% of its workforce in the country, under a reorganisation plan, it said on Friday.

headline: Tibet quake highlights earthquake risk for dams on roof of the world
summary: Tibet's earthquake of magnitude 6.8 that killed 126 and damaged four water reservoirs this week highlights the risks from a hydropower building spree by Asian giants China and India in one of the world's most remote, quake-prone regions, experts say.

headline: Exclusive: US lobbied Greenland rare earths developer Tanbreez not to sell to China
summary: U.S. and Danish officials lobbied the developer of Greenland's largest rare earths deposit last year not to sell its project to Chinese-linked firms, its CEO told Reuters, adding it has been in regular talks with Washington as it reviews funding options to develop the island's critical minerals.

headline: UK inflation expectations rise in December, Citi/YouGov survey shows
summary: British households' expectations for inflation rose in December, according to a survey published on Thursday that may add to concerns among investors about the slow pace of future interest rate cuts by the Bank of England.

headline: Benin army suffers heavy losses in northern attack
summary: Benin's armed forces have suffered heavy losses in an attack on one of their most well-equipped positions in the north, where troops are trying to curb cross-border assaults by Islamist militants, the national guard's chief of staff said on Thursday.

headline: Southwest Airlines' CFO Tammy Romo to retire on April 1
summary: Southwest Airlines on Thursday said Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Tammy Romo will retire from the role effective April 1, after more than three decades with the airline.

headline: Volvo CEO says plan for Mexico truck factory ongoing despite US tariff threat
summary: Sweden's Volvo Group is proceeding with its planned $700-million heavy-truck factory in Monterrey, Mexico, CEO Martin Lundstedt told Reuters on Wednesday, even as President-elect Donald Trump threatens to impose U.S. tariffs on imports of vehicles and other goods.

headline: Constellation Energy nearing $30 billion deal to acquire Calpine, sources say
summary: Constellation Energy is nearing a roughly $30 billion deal to acquire power producer Calpine, people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday, a move that would significantly expand Constellation's generation assets at a time of rising U.S. power demand.

headline: Israeli military tightens media rules over war crimes prosecution concern
summary: The Israeli military placed new restrictions on media coverage of soldiers on active combat duty amid growing concern at the risk of legal action against reservists travelling abroad over allegations of involvement in war crimes in Gaza.

headline: Shareholders urge UnitedHealth to analyze impact of healthcare denials
summary: UnitedHealth Group shareholders on Wednesday said they requested the company prepare a report on the costs and public health impact related to its "practices that limit or delay access to healthcare."

headline: Jefferies' profit jumps on investment banking windfall
summary: Jefferies Financial's profit more than tripled in the fourth quarter as the investment bank earned higher fees from advising on deals and underwriting activity remained strong, it reported on Wednesday.

headline: German real estate deals edge up in 2024, 2025 still seen muted
summary: A key indicator of the health of Germany's property sector improved last year and will make modest gains in 2025, though the next twelve months will continue to be challenging, reports by two major real estate firms said on Wednesday.

headline: Euro zone households likely to keep saving to rebuild wealth, ECB says
summary: Euro zone households could keep saving a large portion of their income to rebuild wealth lost to high inflation, the European Central Bank argued, suggesting lacklustre consumption will continue to weigh on growth in the near term.

headline: EU will not tolerate attacks on its borders, France says after Trump Greenland comments
summary: The European Union will not let other nations attack its sovereign borders, France's foreign minister said on Wednesday, responding to comments by U.S. President-elect Donald Trump on taking over Greenland.

headline: Indonesia signs deal with Qatar investor to build 1 million affordable homes
summary: Indonesia's government signed on Wednesday a memorandum of understanding with an investor from Qatar to build one million affordable homes, one of President Prabowo Subianto's flagship programmes.

headline: Venezuela's Maduro says two US citizens arrested among group of 'mercenaries'
summary: Two U.S. citizens have been arrested in Venezuela, part of a group of seven who President Nicolas Maduro on Tuesday branded as "mercenaries," in the latest roundup ahead of the embattled leader's expected inauguration to a new term later this week.

headline: Australian Open 2025: Who are the other men's contenders to look out for?
summary: Contenders for the men's singles title at the Australian Open, which starts on Sunday:

headline: Canadian dollar consolidates prior day's gains as election looms
summary: The Canadian dollar edged lower against its U.S. counterpart on Tuesday as American economic data supported bets for a slower pace of interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve, but the currency kept hold of much of the previous day's gains.

headline: Turkey says it will mount offensive against Kurdish YPG if demands not met
summary: Turkey will carry out a cross-border offensive into northeastern Syria against the Kurdish YPG militia if the group does not meet Ankara's demands, Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Tuesday, while adding that Syria's new rulers must address the issue.

headline: Red Bulls ink Polish striker Wiktor Bogacz to contract
summary: The New York Red Bulls signed Polish striker Wiktor Bogacz from Miedz Legnica to a four-year contract on Tuesday.

headline: ATP roundup: An upset in Adelaide, a day for the ages in Auckland
summary: Serbian Miomir Kecmanovic upset sixth-seeded Alexander Bublik of Kazakhstan 6-4, 6-2 in opening-round action at the Adelaide International in Australia on Tuesday

headline: Eagles OC, QB on same page before wild-card game
summary: Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Kellen Moore did not sound like a coach concerned he could be entering the playoffs without his starting quarterback.

headline: Trump Middle East envoy predicts 'good things' to announce on Gaza hostages before inauguration
summary: President-elect Donald Trump's Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff said on Tuesday he hopes to have good things to report about hostages held by Hamas in Gaza by the time Trump is sworn in as U.S. president on Jan. 20.

headline: Spain's STL to buy luxury fashion house Christian Lacroix
summary: Spain's Sociedad Textil Lonia (STL) is to buy French fashion house Christian Lacroix for an undisclosed sum, the company said on Tuesday.

headline: Jordan and Syria to combat arms and drugs smuggling, Islamic State's resurgence
summary: Jordan and Syria have agreed to form a joint security committee to secure their border, combat arms and drug smuggling and work to prevent the resurgence of Islamic State militants, the Jordanian foreign minister said on Tuesday.

headline: Meta elects UFC CEO Dana White, two others to board
summary: Meta Platforms said on Monday it had elected three new directors to its board, including Dana White, CEO of Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) and close friend of President-elect Donald Trump.

headline: Canada's Suncor says oil and gas production rose in fourth quarter
summary: Canadian oil and gas company Suncor said on Monday it saw higher upstream production and throughput at its refineries in the fourth quarter.

headline: AbbVie cuts 2024 profit forecast on acquisition expenses
summary: AbbVie lowered its 2024 adjusted profit forecast on Monday as the drugmaker incurred $1.6 billion in acquisition expenses related to milestone payments as well as research-and-development costs.

headline: Aaron Rodgers throws four TDs as Jets beat Dolphins
summary: In what might have been the final game of his Hall of Fame career, Aaron Rodgers threw a season-high four touchdown passes and reached a career milestone while leading the host New York Jets to a 32-20 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J.

headline: Irish services new business growth hits nine-month high in December, PMI shows
summary: Irish services sector activity expanded slightly slower in December but growth in new business hit its fastest pace since March and optimism for the coming 12 months improved, a survey showed on Monday.

headline: History maker Maphaka removes Babar as Pakistan battle at Newlands
summary: South Africa’s youngest test debutant Kwena Maphaka took the key wicket of Babar Azam as Pakistan reached 155 for an effective seven wickets at lunch on day three of the second and final test at Newlands on Sunday, trailing their hosts by 460 runs.

headline: Clemson runs win streak to three by beating Cal
summary: Ian Schieffelin led the way with 21 points as host Clemson posted an 80-68 victory over Cal to stay unbeaten in the Atlantic Coast Conference on Saturday night.

headline: Trump appoints lawyer Stanley Woodward to White House role
summary: Donald Trump on Saturday named Stanley Woodward, an attorney who has defended several of the incoming president's top aides and associates as well as people charged in the Jan. 6, 2021 attack, to join his White House legal team.

headline: Malaysia turns back boats carrying 300 Myanmar migrants
summary: Malaysia's coast guard escorted away from its waters two boats carrying almost 300 undocumented Myanmar migrants found in a state of exhaustion for lack of food and water, a top agency official said.

headline: Mylyjael Poteat lifts Virginia Tech over Miami
summary: Mylyjael Poteat scored a career-high 25 points and delivered the go-ahead three-point play in the final seconds to lift Virginia Tech past visiting Miami 86-85 on Saturday in Blacksburg, Va.

headline: Arteta rues dropped points, Nwaneri injury as Arsenal held
summary: Arsenal's costly 1-1 Premier League draw at Brighton & Hove Albion on Saturday was compounded by an injury to 17-year-old goal-scorer Ethan Nwaneri as coach Mikel Arteta blamed simple mistakes for his side dropping points.

headline: Spurs boss Postecoglou has no problem with Maddison's darts outing
summary: Tottenham Hotspur manager Ange Postecoglou said he had no issues with James Maddison going to watch the PDC World Darts Championship just hours after the midfielder could not start in their 2-2 home draw with Wolverhampton Wanderers due to illness.

headline: Blinken heads to South Korea, Japan and France
summary: U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken will travel to South Korea, Japan and France from Jan. 4-9, the State Department said on Friday, amid a political crisis in Seoul.

headline: KPMG plans new US legal business under Arizona program
summary: Accounting giant KPMG is moving to launch a new legal services business in the United States, taking advantage of relaxed law firm ownership rules in Arizona.

headline: Threat of tariffs will loom large amid auto, tech glitz at CES
summary: Auto and tech giants showing off their latest innovations at the CES trade show in Las Vegas next week can expect a barrage of questions on a topic that is usually not central to the consumer-focused event: tariffs.

headline: European stocks dip at the end of holiday-shortened week
summary: European stocks dipped at the end of a holiday-shortened week on Friday, with traders focussed on economic data for clues on the path of interest rates and potential changes in U.S. policies under a Donald Trump presidency.

headline: Tesla's China sales rise to record high in 2024, bucking global decline
summary: U.S. electric vehicle maker Tesla said on Friday its sales rose 8.8% to a record high of more than 657,000 cars in 2024, a strong performance in a competitive market in a year when its annual global deliveries fell for the first time.

headline: Revs transfer F Esmir Bajraktarevic, sign F Luis Diaz
summary: The New England Revolution said farewell to Esmir Bajraktarevic and signed fellow forward Luis Diaz on Thursday.

headline: Nigeria to expand credit access to citizens
summary: Nigeria will establish a national credit guarantee company in May to lend to businesses and individuals, President Bola Tinubu said in an speech on Wednesday.

headline: India's Mahindra logs 18% jump in Dec car sales to dealers on strong SUV demand
summary: Indian automaker Mahindra & Mahindra said on Wednesday it clocked an 18% jump in sport utility vehicle sales to dealers in December due to strong demand.
